objective: HUB-DIMENSION-20261024-001 found that symmetric edge-bit laws see a three-manifold only through |H1(M; Z2)| and that the Fibonacci rule needs a negative weight; NATIVE-APPROX-20261024-001 identified the six open knots as the Fibonacci knot with a twist, a signed reflection in the Fibonacci basis. Ask whether twists let bits see more of three dimensions: classify the counting laws on ordered triangulations, with any triangle rule read in vertex order (the twisted Fibonacci knots included) and any tetrahedron rule, possibly depending on orientation, under ordered 2-3 and 1-4 moves; and decide whether positive state-sum weights with the twisted Fibonacci support exist. Hypothesis under test: twists add nothing; only the seven symmetric laws survive, and the sign survives the twist. Nearest known work: Turaev-Viro and Dijkgraaf-Witten state sums on ordered triangulations; intrinsic sign problems of topological phases (Smith, Golan and Ringel). Standalone value: whether counting, with or without twists, can see three-dimensional space beyond mod-2 cohomology.
status: Complete 2026-10-25: twists in three dimensions. On ordered triangulations, twists and orientations add nothing to counting laws with one bit per edge: exactly the seven symmetric laws survive the ordered moves, so counts see only |H1(M; Z2)|. In Turaev-Viro form positive weights for the Fibonacci and twisted Fibonacci rules cannot have full support and are pure gauge on the parity class: the sign survives the twist. Next: patterns of patterns in three dimensions (2/3); execution deferred to the owner.
title: Twists in three dimensions
